angle_hi: नान्यगामिना, कहीं और न भटकने वाला

en.intro: Listen closely for one word, and you will hear how Krishna describes the exact state of mind that reaches the supreme divine at the moment of death.
en.notice: Listen for nanyagamina, meaning not going elsewhere. A mind trained by steady practice and fixed on nothing else reaches the supreme person at the moment of death.
en.next: Krishna turns to the nature of the supreme person, who is beyond thought and radiant like the sun.
en.meaning: One who departs while remembering the divine person with a mind trained by practice and fixed on nothing else reaches that supreme divine being, O Partha.

hi.intro: एक शब्द पर ध्यान दीजिए, और आप सुनेंगे कि कृष्ण मृत्यु के समय परम दिव्य तक पहुँचने वाली मन की सटीक स्थिति का वर्णन कैसे करते हैं।
hi.meaning: हे पृथानन्दन, अभ्यासयोग से युक्त और अन्य का चिंतन न करने वाले चित्त से परम दिव्य पुरुष का चिंतन करता हुआ शरीर छोड़ने वाला मनुष्य उसी को प्राप्त हो जाता है।
hi.notice: नान्यगामिना का अर्थ है कहीं और न जाना। जिस मन को अभ्यास से प्रशिक्षित किया गया है और जो किसी और चीज़ पर नहीं भटकता, वह मृत्यु के समय परम पुरुष तक पहुँच जाता है।
hi.next: कृष्ण अब परम पुरुष के स्वरूप की बात करते हैं, जो विचार से परे है और सूर्य के समान तेजस्वी है।

Krishna turns to the nature of the supreme person, who is beyond thought and radiant like the sun.

wrong_fact: "Listen for नान्यगामिना, meaning not going elsewhere. A mind that has been trained by steady practice and is fixed on nothing else but the divine reaches the supreme person at the moment of death." (The word 'नान्यगामिना' means 'not going elsewhere', which matches the source. However, the phrase 'fixed on nothing else but the divine' contradicts the source meaning, which explicitly states 'fixed on nothing else' (नान्यगामिना), meaning the mind is fixed on nothing at all (no other object), rather than being fixed on 'the divine'. This adds a meaning not present in the source.)

borrowed: "Now Krishna speaks of the wise, ancient ruler who is subtler than the subtle and supports all." (The 'next' description for the English intro incorrectly presents the content of verse 9 (which describes the wise ancient ruler) as if it were in verse 8.)
